messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] ap-east-1 detected elevated 502/504 rate and p95 latency for Hosted API + Dedicated pools. Triggered 5180001220. Oncall paged.

alice: seeing a wave of TLS handshake failures at the NLBs -> targets returning handshake_failure / connection reset. Also Datadog forwarder showing large queue and timeouts.

ben: paging @sarah oncall — please jump in. :rotating_light:

sarah: oncall here, taking this. Starting runbook now. @alice please capture the recent ELB logs and target health.

alice: pasted condensed ELB tail:
```
[2026-03-17T02:00:05Z] TLS alert 40 from 10.0.7.42 -> reset
[2026-03-17T02:00:06Z] HTTP/1.1 502 from target i-0a1b2c -> handshake_failure
[2026-03-17T02:01:12Z] connection reset by peer
[2026-03-17T02:02:30Z] client TLS handshake timeout
```

raj: hypothesis: partial NLB cert/cipher roll triggered by provider or infra change. A subset of targets using newer TLS stack are failing. Datadog backlog is compounding — metrics/alerts delayed and autoscaler sees stale metrics.

maria: customer impact: approx 5–7% elevated 5xx for requests originating in ap-east-1. p95 latency jumped from ~180ms -> 1.1–1.3s. Some Dedicated pools reporting model-init stalls and sporadic failed starts. Regional-pinned customers impacted.

sarah: immediate mitigations I am authorizing:
- Enable gateway routing fallback: direct new requests from ap-east-1 -> ap-northeast-1 (gradual then 100%).
- Spillover dedicated reserved capacity to us-east-1 for burst processing.
- Drain and recycle suspect targets in ap-east-1 target groups.
- Throttle or pause Datadog forwarder to reduce ingestion backlog; switch to local short-term metrics proxy for autoscaler.

ben: applying routing fallback rule now:
```
POST /admin/routing/fallback
{ "from": "ap-east-1", "to": "ap-northeast-1", "mode": "force", "percent": 100 }
```

alice: starting targeted drain on tg ap-east-1-tg-3; replacing hosts that show tls_err flag. Command: `./bin/host-replace --tg ap-east-1-tg-3 --filter tls_err` -> started at 5180001290.

raj: quick config tweak pushed: temporarily re-enable legacy TLS ciphers on affected NLB listeners while we validate cert state. AWS CLI used: `aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn ${ARN} --ssl-policy ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01` (rolling).

maria: status page update drafted: small percentage of errors affecting ap-east-1, mitigations underway, next update in 30 minutes or when service is healthy.

sarah: operational notes for handoff: if errors >1% after routing fallback, escalate to eng-runtime + infra for immediate rollback of listener changes and coordinated cert rollback. If Datadog queue >60s, disable autoscaler alarm writes and perform manual scale based on short-term proxies.

ben: confirm fallback is active and traffic is shifting. Observability shows streaming check flaps (websocket sessions) — likely due to client stickiness to drained hosts. Working session migration.

alice: to speed migration, reducing session affinity TTL on NLB/ALB to 30s so clients reattach to fallback endpoints. Command: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn ${TG} --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false` (temporary).

raj: rolled cipher policy change on 4/6 problematic targets so far; handshake failures dropped ~70% on those hosts. Two targets still showing handshake spikes and require service process recycle.

maria: posted status update at 5180001400. Customers notified; support queue flagged for higher priority.

sarah: handing off to night oncall @ben at 5180004200. Current snapshot: error rate from ~6% -> ~1.4%, p95 from ~1.2s -> ~420ms. Dedicated spillover in effect. Next oncall checklist: watch TLS handshake recurrence, confirm Datadog backlog drains <15s, verify dedicated model starts stable.

ben: acknowledged and taking over monitoring. Eng-runtime and infra have been tagged for post-incident follow-up to audit cert rollout and NLB listener changes. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated -> monitoring. severity=high. timestamp window 5180001220 - 5180004567.
